clue.text: Shake bottle men use to produce overall effect

indicators.note: to shake things up is to jumble them, so these letters are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions for shaking a bottle so that the men present achieve a combined result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shake' rearranges BOTTLE MEN USE into the answer; 'to produce' is the link. TOUT ENSEMBLE is a French phrase borrowed into English, used of art and dress.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means the whole taken together, the general impression a work or outfit makes.

clue.text: Screw up a so-called giant

indicators.note: so-called suggests a name as spoken, so the word for giant is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a titan is a giant, from the Greek gods of that name

explanation.surface: Someone crumples up a so-called giant, or bungles one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screw up' looks like 'make a mess of', but here it means turn a screw tighter. 'so-called' signals that TITAN is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: To screw something up, as a nut or a lid, is to make it more firmly fastened.

clue.text: Club loses money to start with, say

indicators.note: loses tells us something is dropped from the golf club's name
to start with places the dropped piece at the front of the word

parts.note: a putter is a golf club used on the green
P is penny, a small coin, so money

explanation.surface: A club that loses cash at the outset, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' suggests a society short of funds, but it is the golf club PUTTER, which loses its first letter P (penny).
explanation.definitionFit: To utter something is to speak it, a synonym of the verb say.

clue.text: Withers wrung by the French, formerly

indicators.note: wrung means twisted, so the letters are twisted into a new arrangement

parts.note: le is the masculine form of 'the' in French

explanation.surface: A horse's withers twisted by Frenchmen in days gone by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Withers' looks like a verb, but it is the ridge between a horse's shoulder blades; 'by' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Erstwhile is an old-fashioned adverb meaning in former times, a synonym of previously.

clue.text: Soaks up sweat

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to wet something is to soak it, so soaks gives wets

explanation.surface: A cloth mops up perspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soaks up' looks like one phrasal verb, but 'up' is the reversal sign working on WETS.
explanation.definitionFit: To stew is to fret anxiously, as in 'let him stew', the same idiom as letting someone sweat.

clue.text: The devil's rewritten this poem

indicators.note: something rewritten has its contents rearranged, so the letters of these words are reordered

explanation.surface: A poet's satanic verses have been redrafted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewritten' rearranges THIS POEM; the 's after devil stands for 'has', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Mephisto is short for Mephistopheles, the demon of the Faust legend, so a name for a devil.

clue.text: Balance the books, omitting the bottom line

indicators.note: omitting signals that part of the word for books is left off

parts.note: a library is a collection of books
RY is railway, a line; it is at the bottom because this is a down clue

explanation.surface: An accountant balances the ledgers but leaves out the final figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Balance the books' reads as accountancy, but 'Balance' is the definition and 'the books' is LIBRARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Libra is the zodiac sign of the scales, the pair of pans used for weighing.

clue.text: Eligible people have an admirer

parts.note: a parti is a person seen as a good match in marriage; partis is the plural
taken as written

explanation.surface: Eligible bachelors and spinsters each have someone who fancies them.
explanation.walkthrough: PARTI, from French, is an eligible person on the marriage market; 'have' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan is a devoted supporter of a cause or person, close in sense to an enthusiast who looks up to them.

clue.text: One presenting a cheque to a native servant

definitions.meaning: the person who holds and hands in a cheque payable to whoever carries it
in British India, a household manservant or porter

explanation.surface: Someone hands a cheque over to a local servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is the link between two senses. The second is a word from the British Raj for an Indian servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheque may be payable to whoever holds it, and in colonial India the word also named a personal attendant or porter.

clue.text: Became PM — accordingly, about to lose all feeling

parts.note: became gives got, as in got angry

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the prime minister's name and the word for accordingly are read backwards together

parts.note: Robert Peel was a British Prime Minister
so means therefore, accordingly

explanation.surface: Someone becomes Prime Minister and is promptly numb with shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Became PM' looks like a political event, but 'PM' is Sir Robert Peel, a 19th-century Prime Minister. 'about' gives OSLEEP; 'to' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A limb that has gone numb from pressure is said to have fallen asleep, so it loses sensation.

clue.text: Warrior, against entering bank

indicators.note: entering means going into, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a brae is a Scots word for a hillside or bank
V is versus, against

explanation.surface: A fighter opposed to breaking into a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: BRAE is Scottish for a slope or riverbank; 'entering' puts V (versus) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A brave is a Native American warrior, an old term from frontier stories.

clue.text: Intentionally lost a little time in the place

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a town is a place, as in 'the whole place knows'
HR is an hour, a short stretch of time

explanation.surface: Someone loses a little time in town on purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intentionally lost' suggests a wasted afternoon, but it describes a match deliberately lost.
explanation.definitionFit: A game or fight that is thrown has been deliberately lost, often for a bribe.

clue.text: Calamity resulting from girl's bloomer

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana, with the possessive s
a flower is a bloomer, and an aster is a flower

explanation.surface: A disaster caused by a young woman's embarrassing slip-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a blunder, but it is a flower, ASTER; 'resulting from' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A disaster is a sudden misfortune, a synonym of catastrophe.

clue.text: Dummy unit, with no sides

indicators.note: no sides means the outermost letters of the run are cut away, leaving what sits inside it

explanation.surface: A mannequin built as a single piece without any side panels.
explanation.walkthrough: Run 'unit, with' together and remove its first and last letters, U and H; what is left sits inside those words.
explanation.definitionFit: Dummy is slang for a fool, a synonym of idiot.

clue.text: Try to carry long packing-case

indicators.note: to carry is to hold within, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: to test is to try out
to long for is to ache for, yearn

explanation.surface: An attempt to lift a lengthy crate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' looks like an adjective describing the case, but it is the verb meaning yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea chests were wooden boxes for shipping tea, widely reused as packing boxes for moving house.

clue.text: It's a more complicated spray

indicators.note: complicated means tangled, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A description of an aerosol as fancier than the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complicated' rearranges IT'S A MORE.
explanation.definitionFit: An atomiser is a device for turning perfume or liquid into a fine mist, a spray bottle.

clue.text: When the carnival finishes, I drink up and almost split

indicators.note: in a down clue, up turns the words before it so they read from the bottom

parts.note: a dram is a measure of whisky, a drink

indicators.note: almost means one letter short, so the end of the word is dropped

parts.note: to grass or split on someone is to inform on them

explanation.surface: A reveller at carnival's end, drinking up and nearly bursting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' gives MARDI and 'almost' cuts the last letter. 'split' is slang for informing, as is the British 'grass'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mardi Gras is Shrove Tuesday, the climax and last day of carnival before Lent begins.

clue.text: Risk a wet tumble

indicators.note: a tumble is a fall, and here the letters before it fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone takes the chance of a soaking fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tumble' rearranges RISK A WET, and the whole clue also describes the sport, where falls end in the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Being towed behind a boat on skis means any fall lands you in the water.

clue.text: Pub frequented by astronauts? No, it's used by typists

definitions.meaning: a whimsical bar out among the stars, where space travellers would drink
the long key at the bottom of a keyboard

explanation.surface: Someone proposes a drinking spot for astronauts, then corrects it to a keyboard item.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a joke reading of the two words; 'No' rejects it in favour of the real meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The long key that puts gaps between words is named for the blank space it inserts, and a bar is a pub.

clue.text: A bird comes second to one's family

parts.note: I is one in Roman numerals, with the possessive s
kin means family, relatives

explanation.surface: A bird ranks second only to its own family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The siskin is a small yellow-green finch of Europe and Asia.

clue.text: Love to order fruit

parts.note: O is love, a zero score in tennis
to range is to arrange in rows or order

explanation.surface: Someone who adores ordering fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: The orange is a citrus fruit.

clue.text: Section of the church overturned set doctrine

indicators.note: overturned means turned upside down, so in a down clue the word is read upwards

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church
to gel is to set, as jelly does

explanation.surface: A church faction has thrown over established teaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' gives EVAN; the surface suggests a breakaway sect.
explanation.definitionFit: An evangel is a gospel, a body of teaching preached as good news.

clue.text: Glass vessel

definitions.meaning: a large drinking glass, for sherry or beer
a sailing ship with fore-and-aft rigged masts

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a tall beer or sherry glass and a two-masted sailing ship.

clue.text: I, so to speak, choose — I start to compare

parts.note: to opt is to choose

indicators.note: start to means the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone muses that when they choose, they begin by comparing.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'I' is the eye, heard rather than seen; the second 'I' is the letter itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Optic is a jocular word for an eye, and the eye is spoken the same as I.

clue.text: Name-dropping best before a celebration

indicators.note: dropping means letting fall, so a letter is removed from the word for best

parts.note: finest means best

explanation.surface: Showing off famous acquaintances is ideal before a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Name-dropping' reads as boasting of acquaintances, but it means N is dropped from FINEST; 'before' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiesta is a festival or holiday, especially a Spanish or Latin American saint's day.

clue.text: Make good money in bar

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: save means except, as bar does in 'all bar one'
L stands for pounds, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Earning a decent amount in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub, but it means except, SAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To salve is to remedy or put right, as in salving a wounded conscience.

clue.text: Clout in row

definitions.meaning: influence or sway, as in having clout with the boss
to work an oar, propelling a boat

explanation.surface: A blow struck during a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means influence or leverage, and also the stroke of an oar through water.

clue.text: An added page — it contains three points

indicators.note: contains means holds within, so the first word wraps round the other

parts.note: N, S and E are three points of the compass

explanation.surface: A supplementary page that includes three main arguments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'points' suggests arguments, but here it is compass points N, S, E.
explanation.definitionFit: An inset is an extra leaf or section placed inside a publication.

clue.text: He's on the field, just on

parts.note: square means fair, just, as in a square deal
the leg side in cricket is also called the on side

explanation.surface: A man stands on a field, only just.
explanation.walkthrough: SQUARE LEG is a cricket fielding position level with the batsman on the leg (on) side.
explanation.definitionFit: Square leg is a cricket fielder placed level with the batter, so a player out in the field.

clue.text: A cold fish, embracing woman, shows weakness

parts.note: a chill is a cold

indicators.note: embracing means holding in the arms, so one word is placed around the other

parts.note: the eel is a fish
she refers to a woman

explanation.surface: An unfriendly person hugging a woman reveals a vulnerable spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cold fish' looks like an aloof person, but it is two pieces, CHILL and EEL; 'shows' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek hero was invulnerable except at his heel, so the phrase names a fatal flaw.
